questions.question: What is Spokane's longstanding nickname, inspired by a flower that thrives in its climate?
questions.explanation: Spokane has been known as "The Lilac City" since the early 1900s. The annual Lilac Festival has been held every May since 1938.

questions.question: Spokane's downtown was rebuilt with stone and brick after which 1889 disaster?
questions.explanation: The Great Spokane Fire of August 4, 1889 destroyed 32 blocks of the downtown business district. The city rebuilt with stone and brick — much of which still stands today.

questions.question: Expo '74 in Spokane was the first World's Fair in history to officially focus on which theme?
questions.explanation: Expo '74's official theme was "Celebrating Tomorrow's Fresh, New Environment" — the first environmentally themed World's Fair. Riverfront Park was created from the fair site after it ended.

questions.question: What annual 7.46-mile Spokane road race draws roughly 50,000 participants on the first Sunday of May?
questions.explanation: Bloomsday was started in 1977 by Olympic marathoner Don Kardong. It's one of the largest timed road races in the world.

questions.question: Which annual Spokane event held the last weekend of June is billed as the world's largest 3-on-3 basketball tournament?
questions.explanation: Hoopfest takes over 45+ blocks of downtown Spokane every year with thousands of teams. It's been running since 1990.

questions.question: Spokane's beloved Frank's Diner — a popular breakfast spot — is housed inside what kind of converted historic vehicle?
questions.explanation: Frank's Diner is built inside a 1906 Northern Pacific railroad observation car — one of only a handful still serving as a working diner anywhere in the country.
